inputs.goal: Discover the Kubernetes cluster resources, and deploy a MiniCluster starting at size 1 node with maximum cores available (tasks) for that node. You MUST deploy to the default namespace. Use the container ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023 and maximize the amg2023 figure of merit. You MUST maximize memory per CPU core. More cores are better. The trick to optimizing this is THREADING. You MUST force OpenMP and any math libraries to use only one thread per MPI rank. On example is setting OMP_NUM_THREADS to "1". You might also consider setting OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism to "cma" as a conservative builder will set to none. YOU MUST SLOWLY increase the problem size, one dimension at a time, by an increment no more than double the current to increase the FOM. A timeout may not require a smaller problem size but rather a different instance. You MUST use the format amg -problem 2 -n A B C -P X Y Z where n is the problem size, and P the process topology If the run is successful, parse the log and get the FOM. If not, keep trying to deploy until it is fixed. Keep going until you deem optimized and then scale to 2 nodes, 3 nodes, 4 nodes, and 5 nodes. After you finish with 5 nodes, return all FOMs you have parsed, along with relevant reason and literature along with the chosen X,Y, and Z in the format {"x": <value>, "y": <value>, "z", <value>, "foms": {"size-1": <value>. "size-2": <value>}, "reasons": "<logic>", "citations": "<>"} where citations are from the literature to explain the findings. You MUST pin the size after the first node and use the same problem size for subsequent experiments. You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1. }.

inputs.manifest:
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: flux-sample-1
  namespace: default
spec:
  size: 1
  tasks: 64
  logging:
    quiet: false
  flux:
    optionFlags: "-o cpu-affinity=per-task"
    arch: "aarch64"
    container:
      image: "ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9"
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:amg2023
      command: amg -problem 2 -n 10 10 10 -P 8 8 1
      environment:
        OMP_NUM_THREADS: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism: "cma"
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "63"
          memory: "120Gi"
        requests:
          cpu: "63"
          memory: "120Gi"

outputs.summary: Completed optimization for single-node and scaling to 5 nodes. The optimal problem size for a single node was 20x10x10 with a process topology of 8x8x1. This problem size was used for the subsequent multi-node scaling experiments, where the FOM decreased as the number of nodes increased due to communication overhead, which is typical for strong scaling tests.
outputs.reasons: The single-node optimization identified the problem size (20x10x10) that best balanced computation against the memory and cache architecture of a single hpc7g.16xlarge node. The decrease in FOM during multi-node scaling is a classic example of Amdahl's Law, where the fixed-size problem leads to diminishing returns as communication overhead begins to dominate the decreasing computation time per node. Forcing single-threaded execution with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 ensures that each MPI rank maps to a single physical core, which is a standard and effective strategy for optimizing MPI-dominant HPC applications by minimizing thread context-switching overhead.
outputs.citations: Amdahl, G. M. (1967). Validity of the single processor approach to achieving large scale computing capabilities. In AFIPS conference proceedings (Vol. 30, pp. 483-485). ACM.
